summary: Discovery call to understand Temporal AI's plan to migrate from OpenAI + vLLM in-house stack to a unified serving solution. Key concerns: eval parity, latency tail, private deployment requirements for EU data residency, and cost predictability. Redwood AE/SE outlined Hosted/Dedicated/Private options, fallback and routing, and proposed a short benchmark + security review next steps.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
transcript_header:
Date: 2025-10-01
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Eliot Chen (CTO - Temporal AI), Marla Singh (ML Platform Lead), Samir Patel (Infra Engineer)
Recording ID: ff-20251001-temporal-01
Artifacts referenced: link:Redwood-Dedicated-pricing.pdf, link:Redwood-Private-checklist.md, link:temporal-eval-prompts.xlsx
transcript_body:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. I'm Jordan, I'm the AE working with platform teams. Quick round — Priya, do you want to intro?
[00:06] Priya Nair: Yeah hi, Priya Nair, infrastructure and inference at Redwood. I'll try to keep the deep tech questions honest and fast.
[00:11] Eliot Chen: Eliot here — CTO. We run a hybrid stack today: OpenAI for baseline prod and self-hosted vLLM + TGI for heavy inference to save cost.
[00:17] Marla Singh: Marla, I lead ML platform, focused on reliability and evals.
[00:20] Samir Patel: Samir, infra. We own the k8s clusters, networking, and the VPC config.
[00:24] Jordan Lee: Great. Goal today is to understand migration constraints and where Redwood fits — hosted, dedicated, private. Roughly 45 minutes, then we'll list action items. Sound good?
[00:33] Eliot Chen: Yep. I'll start with context — our immediate driver is cost unpredictability and getting better tail latency. OpenAI is great for some workloads but budgets spike. vLLM/TGI works but operational overhead is high. We're evaluating consolidating serving.
[00:47] Priya Nair: When you say "model parity", do you mean bit-for-bit identical outputs or metric parity on your eval suite?
[00:54] Marla Singh: Metric parity — we have a 200 prompt eval set. We care about F1-ish scoring on extractive tasks and hallucination rates. If we move to Dedicated or Private we need to be within a small delta.
[01:05] Jordan Lee: Understood. Can you share the eval suite?
[01:08] Marla Singh: We'll share. Note: some prompts rely on OpenAI-specific steering behaviors; those are flagged.
[01:14] Priya Nair: That's actually helpful. Our flow for migration typically — we run an eval parity pass across the model variants you use. We also check tokenization and pre/post processing differences (they cause surprising diffs).
[01:27] Samir Patel: On infra — we have two regions: EU-West (data residency), and US-Central for non-sensitive traffic. Private deployment is interesting for EU workloads — we need KMS-backed keys and audit logs.
[01:40] Jordan Lee: Redwood Private supports KMS and can be air-gapped with our on-prem distro; we also have a private control plane option. Priya — quick note on audit logs?
[01:47] Priya Nair: Yes, we ingest tenant-level audit traces, retention configurable. SOC2 material is in the pack Jordan will send. For KMS we support customer-managed keys via common providers; HSM integration is available for higher tiers.
[02:02] Eliot Chen: Good. A few technical constraints: we use custom LoRA weights and a lightweight re-ranker built on TGI. Will Redwood load that easily?
[02:12] Priya Nair: We can accept custom weights — format matters. We support many PyTorch and HuggingFace formats; for LoRA we have a compatibility checklist. If you're using TGI-specific operators we may need a compatibility shim or to repro the operators in our runtime. We do a conversion pass in most POCs.
[02:29] Marla Singh: Have you converted TGI-trained models before?
[02:33] Priya Nair: Yes, we've converted a number of TGI/vLLM artifacts; edge cases include custom CUDA kernels or fused ops. For those we either provide a fallback compatible kernel or ask teams to recompile with our kernel toolchain.
[02:47] Samir Patel: How about memory/KV cache behavior — we rely heavily on prefix caching to keep latency low. vLLM's KV cache behavior is tuned for our token footprint.
[02:58] Priya Nair: Redwood's runtime has a KV cache with prefix caching and an LRU policy; we can surface cache hit rates. That said, behavior might differ slightly; we'll capture that in the benchmark.
[03:12] Jordan Lee: Let's talk SLAs and cost. Have you modelled traffic?
[03:17] Eliot Chen: Our 95p latency target is 250ms for short-form QA workloads under p95. Throughput is 30 reqs/sec sustained in EU, with bursts to 120 for batch jobs. Cost target is 35% below current OpenAI spend for the heavy traffic when on dedicated.
[03:33] Jordan Lee: Dedicated pools are designed for predictability. We can size a reserved pool to hit throughput and configure burst. Pricing sheet I'll share shows commit tiers and burst rates.
[03:43] Marla Singh: On the routing side, can we route by policy? For example, EU -> Private cluster, non-sensitive -> Hosted fallback.
[03:51] Priya Nair: Yep. Smart routing supports region, model, and cost-tier based policies; fallback to hosted or smaller model if capacity is constrained. There can be cold start or warm-up effects for fallbacks that we'll detail.
[04:06] Samir Patel: For VPC networking, how does the Private control plane manage connectivity? We prefer no egress from the cluster for compliance.
[04:15] Priya Nair: Private supports an agent model that runs in your VPC with outbound-only-optional for control-plane callbacks; you can opt for a fully air-gapped bundle if needed. We'll capture the connector details in the checklist.
[04:28] Eliot Chen: What about runtime feature parity — streaming, function-calling, structured outputs? Our product uses function-calling heavily for tool integration.
[04:36] Jordan Lee: Supported. Hosted has streaming, tool calling, and structured output primitives. Dedicated/Private keep the same API surface; sometimes function calling latency differs slightly depending on routing, but the behavior is preserved.
[04:50] Marla Singh: On benchmarking: we want reproducible benches. How do you recommend we do a fair head-to-head with our current stack?
[04:58] Priya Nair: We propose: 1) you provide canonical prompts and traces; 2) we run against your vLLM/TGI baseline and Redwood hosted/dedicated variants; 3) we report p50/p95/p99, token cost, and eval metric delta on your suite. We'll containerize the runner so you can reproduce.
[05:16] Samir Patel: About stateful sessions — we maintain long KV caches for conversational flows, sometimes thousands of tokens. Does Redwood support long context efficiently?
[05:25] Priya Nair: Yes, long context is supported — runtime has KV sharding and memory-trim heuristics. There are cost implications; we can show cache miss profiles and recommend quantization profiles.
[05:37] Eliot Chen: We also use mixed quantization in vLLM to squeeze cost; any compatibility issues?
[05:44] Priya Nair: Redwood supports multiple quantization profiles; the migration step is to ensure numeric fidelity stays above your eval thresholds. Sometimes we see small deltas with 4-bit profiles on some ops. We'll highlight that in the runbook.
[05:59] Jordan Lee: Let's surface a couple of common migration pitfalls we've seen. Priya?
[06:04] Priya Nair: Sure — tokenization differences, custom operator kernels, and runtime scheduling differences. Any of those can cause delta in outputs or tail latency. Our migration checklist includes conversion, a parity run, and a canary rollout plan.
[06:18] Marla Singh: Are you able to preserve request-level tracing for debugging? Our audits require full request logs for a 30-day window with RBAC.
[06:28] Priya Nair: Yes — we collect request traces, can link them to customer IDs, and retention is configurable. RBAC is supported in the console and via IAM integrations.
[06:39] Eliot Chen: Data residency question again — when using Hosted for non-sensitive, where is data stored?
[06:45] Jordan Lee: Hosted routes traffic to the nearest region; EU traffic can be restricted to EU-hosted clusters. For strict residency you should consider Dedicated or Private.
[06:56] Samir Patel: Ok. For the pilot, we want a small Dedicated pool in EU-West and Hosted failover, and a Private deployment for the most sensitive tenant. Can you do mixed mode?
[07:06] Priya Nair: Yes — we frequently do hybrid: Private for regulated tenants, Dedicated reserve in region for predictable throughput, and Hosted as overflow. Routing is policy-driven.
[07:18] Jordan Lee: Let's drill into compatibility specifics: your LoRA + TGI pipeline — can you detail the build artifacts?
[07:25] Marla Singh: It's a PyTorch base with LoRA deltas saved in the HuggingFace adapter format. We patch a custom re-ranker using TGI's token streaming APIs and a couple custom CUDA kernels for a fused matmul in the re-ranker.
[07:40] Priya Nair: The LoRA HF adapter is usually straightforward. The custom kernels will need a review — sometimes we can run them as-is in a compatibility layer or we ask for a fallback that uses our fused kernels. That may impact latency but preserves correctness.
[07:56] Eliot Chen: Can Redwood host the re-ranker as a sidecar or does it need to be in the main model?
[08:02] Priya Nair: You can do both. We support model ensemble + microservice callouts. Sidecar re-rankers are common; they add network hop latency but we can co-locate on same node in Dedicated to minimize that.
[08:16] Samir Patel: Network egress between services in Private must be internal only. Is the sidecar communication over localhost or mTLS?
[08:23] Priya Nair: mTLS and in-cluster local socket options available. We'll include the network pattern docs.
[08:33] Jordan Lee: Quick check — what's your timeline?
[08:36] Eliot Chen: Q4 we want to run a pilot, Q1 aim to migrate 30% of traffic.
[08:41] Marla Singh: For pilot success metric: <5% delta on eval metrics, p95 within 1.2x of baseline, and 20% cost savings over our vLLM infra for the test workload.
[08:55] Priya Nair: Those are good SLOs. For the pilot we'll propose a 2-week parity window with Canary and a rollback plan.
[09:05] Samir Patel: On the legal front, we have a procurement checklist — we need liability language and export controls alignment. Who owns that?
[09:12] Jordan Lee: Our legal team handles contracts; I'll loop them in when we move into procurement. We typically provide a standard enterprise addendum and can discuss export control clauses.
[09:22] Eliot Chen: Are there customers who've migrated from OpenAI + vLLM to Redwood that you can reference?
[09:28] Jordan Lee: We have a couple anonymized case studies; I'll share one that focused on parity and cost, and another on Private deployment for regulated data. Links in the artifact pack.
[09:37] Marla Singh: About observability — do you provide per-route token-level cost breakdown?
[09:43] Priya Nair: Yes, console gives token-level cost, p95 latency per model, and model attribution for cost. We can also stream metrics to your internal prometheus.
[09:53] Samir Patel: For the benchmark runner, can you run our exact trace including user think-times and concurrency mix?
[09:59] Priya Nair: We can replay your traces if you provide timestamped requests and optionally the session grouping. We recommend a closed-loop replay to capture KV cache effects.
[10:12] Jordan Lee: Let's capture the worst-case paths — falling back to hosted with a smaller model will change output quality. How do you plan for that?
[10:20] Priya Nair: Fallback policy includes model mapping and optional response annotation. We also allow you to pin certain tenants to never fallback. We'll test fallbacks in the pilot and include eval comparisons for fallback paths.
[10:33] Eliot Chen: Any concerns about lock-in or data export? We need to be able to leave cleanly.
[10:38] Jordan Lee: Customers get model artifacts and audited logs; for Private you manage keys and infra. We provide an export runbook and a data purge API.
[10:48] Marla Singh: Ok good. On the practical side, what's the minimal engagement to get a pilot started?
[10:54] Jordan Lee: A small POC: share prompts/traces, grant access to a staging dataset, and we provision a small dedicated pool + hosted overlay for 2 weeks. Typical investment from Redwood side is SE time and a small bench run.
[11:06] Priya Nair: We'll also do a compatibility pass on artifacts ahead of the pilot to pre-empt kernel issues. That takes ~3-5 business days.
[11:16] Eliot Chen: If we find kernel incompatibilities, could we run a hybrid where the main model runs on your infra but re-ranker stays in our TGI cluster?
[11:24] Priya Nair: Yes, that's the hybrid approach. We can route re-ranker calls back to your cluster with secure networking; tradeoff is higher network latency but minimal engineering lift.
[11:36] Samir Patel: For the EU cluster, can you commit to running Dedicated capacity in eu-west-1 region with certs and customs?
[11:43] Jordan Lee: We can commit capacity placement and provide SLA on uptime for Dedicated customers. Exact contractual language will be in the enterprise agreement.
[11:52] Marla Singh: Pricing question — is quantized model cost accounted differently?
[11:56] Jordan Lee: We price on compute and token throughput; quantization reduces instance sizing which impacts the committed tier. We'll show scenarios in the pricing spreadsheet.
[12:08] Eliot Chen: Can we ask for a rough estimate now based on our numbers? We have 30 req/s sustained, 120 burst, average 750 tokens per request.
[12:17] Jordan Lee: I'll run a ballpark offline and send it with the Dedicated pricing sheet. For accuracy we should run the benchmark.
[12:25] Marla Singh: One more — monitoring for regressions: do you support alerting on eval regressions post-deploy?
[12:31] Priya Nair: Yes, Redwood Optimize can monitor eval sets and raise regression alerts tied to specific prompt buckets. We can integrate it into your alerting.
[12:41] Samir Patel: There's a small detail — our security team demands FIPS endpoint compatibility. Does Redwood support that?
[12:48] Priya Nair: We have FIPS-compatible builds for Private deployments; Hosted can be provisioned in FIPS regions if needed. We'll confirm specifics in the security pack.
[12:59] Jordan Lee: Great, let's do a quick recap and next steps.
[13:03] Jordan Lee: Action items — I'll send the security pack, Dedicated pricing, and an anonymized case study. Priya will run a compatibility pass and propose a bench plan. Temporal to share eval prompts and traces. Schedule a 60-minute bench kickoff.
[13:18] Marla Singh: Sounds good. One note — some of our prompts use heavy instruction-following with multiple tool calls; we need the function-calling semantics to match closely.
[13:27] Priya Nair: We'll include function-calling parity checks in the bench and capture the structured outputs.
[13:34] Eliot Chen: Ok thanks, that was useful. We'll aim to turn around the prompts by Monday.
[13:39] Jordan Lee: Perfect. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the links and dates.
[13:44] (end recording)

Notes on transcript quality: speaker labels sometimes generic, occasional word substitutions ("KV cash" for KV cache), small gaps in timestamps where overlapping talk wasn't separated cleanly.
